items.title: Right-wedge Rindler clocks, radial rays and frequency ratio
items.statement:
Use the flat affine Minkowski model with signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and SI coordinates $(x^0,x^1,y,z)=(ct,x^1,y,z)$. Fix $a>0$ in metres per second squared and define

$$\Phi_a(T,\rho,y,z)=\bigl(\rho\sinh(aT/c),\rho\cosh(aT/c),y,z\bigr),\qquad T\in\mathbb R,\quad \rho>0.$$

Then $\Phi_a$ is a smooth chart of the right wedge $W=\{x^1>|x^0|\}$, with $\rho$ in metres and $T$ in seconds. Its pullback metric, the proper-time rate of a stationary Rindler observer, and that observer's proper-acceleration magnitude are

$$ds^2=-\frac{a^2\rho^2}{c^2}\,dT^2+d\rho^2+dy^2+dz^2,\qquad \frac{d\tau}{dT}=\frac{a\rho}{c^2},\qquad \alpha=\frac{c^2}{\rho}.$$

For ideal radial vacuum rays with $y,z$ fixed, $d\rho/dT=\pm a\rho/c$. A ray joining positive radii $\rho_E,\rho_R$ therefore has one-way Rindler travel time $\Delta T=(c/a)|\log(\rho_R/\rho_E)|$, and stationary ideal clocks at those radii satisfy $\Delta\tau_R/\Delta\tau_E=\rho_R/\rho_E$ over any common nonzero $T$ interval. The clock statement is conditional on the ideal-clock adoption in [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]].

For a future null plane-wave covector $k$ directed along the same radial ray, define $\omega_n=-k(U_n)$ using [[def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency]]. The contraction functional obeys $\omega_R/\omega_E=\rho_E/\rho_R$. Reading this as an accelerated-observer reception frequency requires the extra hypothesis [A2] below: clause (iv) of [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]] excludes accelerated-observer reception. The result is conditional and does not silently extend that postulate. The coordinate chart excludes $\rho=0$; no global rigid accelerated frame is asserted.

items.physical_scope: Exact coordinate and proper-time calculations in the right wedge of flat Minkowski spacetime for the stated uniformly accelerated congruence and idealized radial null rays. The clock ratio is conditional on the adopted ideal-clock postulate. The frequency contraction ratio is a mathematical observer-frequency functional; interpreting it as reception by accelerated observers requires the additional hypothesis [A2], which the current plane-wave postulate explicitly excludes. No measurement, material clock model, global accelerated frame, or claim about real clocks or light is asserted.

items.title: Exact relativistic orbit in a uniform electric field
items.statement:
In the flat Minkowski specialization of [[def-rpm-charge-spin-model]], adopt the fixed-endpoint external-charge action [[post-rpm-external-charge-action]] and its conditional stationary-action equivalence [[pthm-rpm-external-charge-action-equivalence]]. Let $m>0$, $q\in\mathbb R$, $c>0$, $E_0\in\mathbb R$, and let the uniform field in one named inertial SI chart be $\mathbf E=E_0e_1$, $\mathbf B=0$. A smooth global potential is $\phi=-E_0x^1$, $\mathbf A=0$, so the local-potential hypothesis is satisfied. Set $F_0=qE_0$ (newtons), take initial event $(0,\mathbf x_0)$ and initial momentum $\mathbf p_0=(p_{01},\mathbf p_\perp)$ at $t=0$, and define

$$p_1(t)=p_{01}+F_0t,\qquad \Pi=\sqrt{m^2c^2+|\mathbf p_\perp|^2}>0,\qquad \mathcal E(t)=c\sqrt{\Pi^2+p_1(t)^2},\qquad \mathbf v(t)=\frac{c(p_1(t)e_1+\mathbf p_\perp)}{\sqrt{\Pi^2+p_1(t)^2}}.$$

If $F_0\ne0$, the exact position for every $t\in\mathbb R$ is

$$x^1(t)=x^1_0+\frac c{F_0}\left(\sqrt{\Pi^2+p_1(t)^2}-\sqrt{\Pi^2+p_{01}^2}\right),$$
$$\mathbf x_\perp(t)=\mathbf x_{\perp0}+\frac{c\mathbf p_\perp}{F_0}\log\!\left(\frac{p_1(t)+\sqrt{\Pi^2+p_1(t)^2}}{p_{01}+\sqrt{\Pi^2+p_{01}^2}}\right).$$

If $F_0=0$, the field exerts no force on the particle and the orbit is free:
$\mathbf p(t)=\mathbf p_0$, $\mathcal E(t)=\mathcal E(0)$ and
$\mathbf x(t)=\mathbf x_0+c^2\mathbf p_0t/\mathcal E(0)$. These formulas define future-timelike worldlines for all finite coordinate times; any model solution with the same data agrees with them on every common connected time interval. This is a conditional model deduction, not evidence that the adopted action describes a measured particle.

items.title: Exact relativistic helix in a uniform magnetic field
items.statement:
Use the flat SI charged-particle model and local external-action adoption of [[def-rpm-charge-spin-model]] and [[post-rpm-external-charge-action]], with the conditional equation and coordinate Lorentz force of [[pthm-rpm-external-charge-action-equivalence]] and [[pthm-rpm-charge-mass-shell]]. Let $m>0$, $q\in\mathbb R$, $c>0$, and $\mathbf E=0$, $\mathbf B=B_0e_3$. The smooth global potential $\phi=0$, $\mathbf A=(-B_0x^2/2,B_0x^1/2,0)$ has $\nabla\times\mathbf A=B_0e_3$. Given initial position $\mathbf x_0$ and momentum $\mathbf p_0=(p_{01},p_{02},p_{03})$ at $t=0$, define

$$S_0=\sqrt{m^2c^2+|\mathbf p_0|^2},\qquad \gamma_0=S_0/(mc),\qquad \Omega=\frac{qB_0}{\gamma_0m}.$$

For $\Omega\ne0$, the exact momentum and energy are

$$p_1(t)=p_{01}\cos(\Omega t)+p_{02}\sin(\Omega t),\quad p_2(t)=p_{02}\cos(\Omega t)-p_{01}\sin(\Omega t),\quad p_3(t)=p_{03},\quad \mathcal E(t)=cS_0,$$

and the exact position is

$$x^1(t)=x^1_0+\frac{c}{S_0\Omega}\bigl(p_{01}\sin(\Omega t)+p_{02}(1-\cos(\Omega t))\bigr),$$
$$x^2(t)=x^2_0+\frac{c}{S_0\Omega}\bigl(p_{02}\sin(\Omega t)-p_{01}(1-\cos(\Omega t))\bigr),\qquad x^3(t)=x^3_0+\frac{cp_{03}}{S_0}t.$$

The transverse projection is a circle of radius $|\mathbf p_\perp|/|qB_0|$ when $\mathbf p_\perp=(p_{01},p_{02})\ne0$; it is a straight line parallel to $e_3$ when $\mathbf p_\perp=0$. If $p_{03}=0$ the circular orbit is planar. The field does no work. If $\Omega=0$ (including $q=0$ or $B_0=0$), the solution is free motion $\mathbf p(t)=\mathbf p_0$, $\mathcal E=cS_0$, $\mathbf x(t)=\mathbf x_0+c\mathbf p_0t/S_0$. These formulas give a global future-timelike orbit and are unique on every common connected time interval; they are conditional model deductions, not empirical claims.

items.title: Subcritical crossed fields and exact drift-frame orbits
items.statement:
In the flat SI charged-particle model with the adopted action and conditional force equation of [[post-rpm-external-charge-action]], [[pthm-rpm-external-charge-action-equivalence]] and [[pthm-rpm-charge-mass-shell]], let $\mathbf E=E_0e_1$, $\mathbf B=B_0e_3$, $B_0\ne0$, and $|E_0|<c|B_0|$. Use the smooth combined potential $\phi=-E_0x^1$, $\mathbf A=(-B_0x^2/2,B_0x^1/2,0)$. Define

$$\mathbf v_d=\frac{\mathbf E\times\mathbf B}{|\mathbf B|^2}=-\frac{E_0}{B_0}e_2,\qquad \gamma_d=(1-|\mathbf v_d|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}.$$

The passive Lorentz boost of velocity $\mathbf v_d$ transforms these fields to $\mathbf E'=0$, $\mathbf B'=\mathbf B/\gamma_d$. Consequently every flat-model solution in the laboratory frame is the inverse boost of the uniform-magnetic-field orbit of [[pthm-rpm-constant-magnetic-helix]] with the boosted initial data. The laboratory coordinate time increases strictly and ranges over all real values along that inverse-boosted orbit. In particular, the constant velocity $\mathbf v=\mathbf v_d$ is an exact solution because $\mathbf E+\mathbf v_d\times\mathbf B=0$. Other initial data give boosted helical orbits; the theorem does not identify every velocity with $\mathbf v_d$. The cases $|E_0|=c|B_0|$ and $|E_0|>c|B_0|$ are outside the statement.

items.physical_scope: Exact conditional flat-space statement for constant perpendicular electric and magnetic fields in the adopted external charged test-particle model. When $|E|<c|B|$, a subluminal passive boost removes the electric field and every solution is the inverse boost of a uniform-magnetic-field orbit. A constant drift-velocity solution is singled out, but the theorem does not claim that all particle velocities equal the drift velocity. Null and supercritical crossed fields are excluded; no self-field, radiation reaction, measurement, or empirical claim is made.

title: Right-wedge accelerated clocks and rays — Examples

examples.title: Two stationary clocks and one radial Rindler pulse
examples.statement: Specialize [[pthm-rpm-rindler-clock-gradient]] to $a=2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$, emission radius $\rho_E=2\,\mathrm m$, reception radius $\rho_R=4\,\mathrm m$, and a future outward radial ray. These are exact model parameters. The one-way coordinate travel time is $(c/2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}})\log 2$, and over a shared Rindler-time interval the ideal-clock ratio is $\Delta\tau_R/\Delta\tau_E=2$. The observer-frequency contraction functional ratio is $\omega_R/\omega_E=1/2$; its interpretation as an accelerated reception frequency is conditional on the unresolved additional hypothesis in the theorem. No experiment is described.

examples.title: Uniform electric field from rest
examples.statement:
Choose $m=1\,\mathrm{kg}$, $q=1\,\mathrm C$, $E_0=2\,\mathrm{N\,C^{-1}}$, $\mathbf B=0$, and initial data $\mathbf x_0=0$, $\mathbf p_0=0$ at $t=0$ in [[pthm-rpm-constant-electric-orbit]]. Then $F_0=2\,\mathrm N$, $p_1(t)=F_0t$, and for every finite $t$ the model orbit is

$$x^1(t)=\frac c{F_0}\left(\sqrt{m^2c^2+F_0^2t^2}-mc\right),\qquad x^2(t)=x^3(t)=0,$$

with $v_1(t)=cF_0t/\sqrt{m^2c^2+F_0^2t^2}$. This is a symbolic model calculation with chosen parameters, not a report of measured field or particle data.

examples.title: A circular magnetic orbit with zero axial momentum
examples.statement:
In [[pthm-rpm-constant-magnetic-helix]], choose $qB_0>0$, $p_{01}=p_*>0$, $p_{02}=p_{03}=0$, and arbitrary $m>0$. Then $S_0=\sqrt{m^2c^2+p_*^2}$, $\gamma_0=S_0/(mc)$ and $\Omega=qB_0/(\gamma_0m)>0$. The orbit is the circle

$$x^1=x^1_0+\frac{cp_*}{S_0\Omega}\sin(\Omega t),\qquad x^2=x^2_0-\frac{cp_*}{S_0\Omega}\bigl(1-\cos(\Omega t)\bigr),\qquad x^3=x^3_0,$$

of radius $p_*/(qB_0)$, with constant energy $cS_0$. At $t=\pi/(2\Omega)$ its momentum is $(0,-p_*,0)$. All values are model parameters, not observations.

examples.title: The exact constant drift solution in subcritical crossed fields
examples.statement: Let $B_0>0$ and set $E_0=cB_0/2$, so $\mathbf E=E_0e_1$, $\mathbf B=B_0e_3$ is subcritical. In [[pthm-rpm-crossed-field-drift]], the drift velocity and boost factor are $\mathbf v_d=-(c/2)e_2$ and $\gamma_d=2/\sqrt3$. The constant-velocity orbit $\mathbf x(t)=\mathbf x_0+\mathbf v_dt$ solves the adopted model for any $m>0$ and constant charge $q$: its Lorentz force vanishes. This is one exact solution; other initial data yield boosted magnetic orbits.
